text:
monitor-bot: ALERT: Nightly perf dashboard detected a p95 latency spike for model-inference-prod (route: /v1/generate). p95 jumped ~120ms (280ms -> 400ms) starting ~2024-06-05T03:00Z. Affected hosts: serve-3a[12-14]. Suspect path: stride-batcher-v2 kernel selection. https://dash.redwood/alerts/5991 :rotating_light:
lia: seeing the same pattern in staging runs — perf job staging-perf-143 failed with p95 +110ms around the same window :eyes:
suresh: I started a local bisect, suspicious commit is PR #8392 (adaptive-batching-stride) merged last night by @jamie. quick grep shows a change to default epsilon in batcher config.:thinking_face:
alex: can you paste the profiler samples / top stacks?
suresh: quick perf top dump from a repro run:
```
perf top -p 22345 -g --nsamples=2000
samples: 36.8%  batcher::stride_handler
15.4%  kernel_selector::score_stride
9.7%   exec::dispatch_kernels
...
```
jamie: yeah i raised epsilon to 0.15 in that PR to reduce small-batch churn (was 0.05). didn't think it would move kernel selection that far.
oncall-ryan: this is affecting prod SLOs — recommend hold rollout and revert PR #8392 in staging & canary immediately. I'll take action if you confirm.
suresh: confirm - bisect pins it to the PR. repro is stable locally.
deploy-bot: Rollback request accepted: reverting PR #8392 to canary and staging. Started deployments to canary/staging (tags: revert/8392). CI: queued perf-suite/staging.
lia: staging perf-suite completed: p95 returned to ~285ms, throughput unchanged. Looks like revert fixed it. :white_check_mark:
alex: next steps: open a perf-regression issue, add a guard to rollout pipeline that blocks if p95 increases >20% vs baseline on canary. also add a small synthetic perf test exercising stride-heavy batches to CI.
suresh: i'll add telemetry for kernel selection weights (histogram) so we can catch weight shifts in metrics. will also drop a short config tweak PR to use a softer epsilon and an A/B experiment before re-rolling.
monitor-bot: ALERT auto-resolved after deployment revert. Root cause flagged: adaptive-batching-stride weight increase caused kernel selector to prefer stride kernels, resulting in higher p95 on common request mix.
jamie: sorry about the regression — will follow up with a postmortem and the experimental rollout plan.
lia: thanks all for quick responses. moving this to triage channel for a short postmortem and action items. :memo:
